  adoption names `agent-files copy --from` and `diff --from`, and `hooks.sh`'s guard test names
  `install --dev`, `build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` being `build`, `install`, and `run`
  with `--dev` now. A rule that says `install-dev` says `install --dev`.
- And then by profile, by **feat: build, install, and run take --profile**: `--dev` retired to
  `--profile dev`, so `hooks.sh`'s guard test names `install --profile dev`, and a rule that says
  `install-dev` or `install --dev` says `install --profile dev`. The `[build]` and `[install]` keys a
  rule might name are `commands`, `dir`, and the `[profile.<name>]` tables.

##### Why: the scope flags

`-s` is required on the write commands and `sync` once **feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and run-dev**
lands, so the rules' invocations must carry it or fail.

#### The closing is a trapezoid or linear, and converts

- A multi-step cycle closes as a trapezoid by default or as linear on request, the closing commit
  carrying the shape, so nothing is reshaped at Land.
  - `vc-x1 commit --closing <BM|REV>`, naming the cycle's tip, onto the trunk, `--land`'s bookmark
    or `[cycle] trunk`, `main` when absent, makes the closing in the shape `--shape
    <trapezoid|linear>` names, else the `.vc-config.md` key `[cycle] closing-shape`, else
    trapezoid, and prints which decided.
  - Trapezoid is the merge of the trunk and the ladder's tip. Linear is a plain commit on the
    ladder, so the trunk carries one commit per rung, the shape the rules called keep separate,
    renamed.
  - The key is the project's preference, so each adopter sets its own, and one that sets nothing
    keeps the trapezoid.
  - Either converts to the other while the closing is a draft, before Land, by re-parenting the
    same closing: its change id, trailer, and, with the trunk unmoved, its tree are kept.
- Land is sync, then `commit --closing <BM|REV> --land [TRUNK]`, the fast-forward and the push,
  then `vc-x1 install`. To test the closing before it is published, it is made without `--land`,
  its release build, the candidate, installed off the PATH by `vc-x1 install --dir <DIR>` and
  tested by its path, and the candidate lands it, `<DIR>/vc-x1 land -s b --onto <TRUNK>`, and
  installs itself, `<DIR>/vc-x1 install`. The fast-forward lands the tree tested, so `cmp
  <DIR>/vc-x1` with the installed binary finds no difference, and the plain `vc-x1` is replaced
  only by what is on the trunk. The bookmark deleted is the one `--closing` names, or for a revision its
  current or nearest parent bookmark above the trunk, several refused with the list, and the
  branch's other bookmarks are left and named as merged. The trapezoid recipe goes,
  Close-out step 5 keeps the user's choice, the key its default, and carries it out by the flag,
  and `jj.md` Close-out shapes names the two shapes and why squash is not a shape.

- The shape's name: with one rung the figure is a triangle, wink's observation (2026-10-20), so
  "trapezoid" names one case. The tool calls the operation `merge` and the result the merge
  close-out, and the rules' text could follow. `commit --closing` merges into the trunk as it is
  now, a bookmark read where it points, so a `main` that moved during the cycle no longer stops Land
  for a rebase. A linear closing cannot join a moved trunk without rewriting the reviewed ladder, so
  its Land refuses one.

##### Why: a trapezoid by default, linear on request

The trapezoid keeps every rung reachable while `git log --first-parent` reads one commit per cycle,
and it joins a moved trunk. Some prefer a straight history, which linear gives, and the choice is
made at the closing, so the shape is in the commit that was reviewed rather than a reshape at Land
made after it. Converting is cheap while the closing is a draft, so the choice is never final
before Land.

#### A cycle's shape is its branch's commit count

- [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)'s "A ladder that shrinks to one rung still closes as a
  ladder" goes: a branch with one commit above the trunk, the opening alone, is a single-step cycle,
  and `commit --closing <BM|REV>` finalizes that commit in place, the bare cycle title replacing the
  opening's, while more commits get the closing commit. Every closing names its tip, by the cycle's
  bookmark or a revision, `@-` the common one, and the count reads the branch, so there is no bare
  form, and `--dead-end` always makes the closing commit.
- Any commit on any line closes: a tip that is not `@-` is closed by a detour, `@` moving onto it
  and returning after, and the commits above it stay as they are.
- A parent wrong after the fact is fixed with `vc-x1 reparent`, never by closing again.
- Every cycle starts with `commit --opening`, a single-step cycle included: its bookmark is created
  and pushed at the trunk, and its one commit begins as the opening, the work squashed into it. So
  Opening step 2, the bookmark's creation and publication by `jj git push`, is `commit --opening`'s,
  and the step names it.
- The closing's title and body may be left out: the cycle title is read from the opening, and the
  body comes from `.vc-config.md`'s `[closing] body`.

##### Why: the commit count

The tool tells the shapes apart by counting, with no title to read, and a cycle need not decide its
shape before its first commit: it is single-step until a second commit makes it a ladder.

#### A commit body is two plain paragraphs

- The problem, then the solution opening "Solution:", ending with the pointer to the record where
  it is at that commit, "See details in zDOING.md." on a rung and "See details in zCLOSED.md." on
  the closing, which moves it, no bullets, and the rung subsection the full account: the entry **A
  commit body is an intro and a pointer to the record** in `## Todo`, its rule, specimens, and
  subsection change. The bookends stay pointers, "Opens the cycle ..." and "Closes the cycle ...",
  with the same pointer after them.

##### Why: two paragraphs

A `git log` reader gets what was wrong and what was done in two sentences, and the breakdown is
written once, in the record, rather than twice.

#### Ladder labels from `[0]`

- `notes.md` and the `cycle-model.md` specimen number the ladder's reference labels from `[0]`.

##### Why: labels from zero

Each label then equals its rung's version suffix.

#### A rung may run the acceptance check

- Close-out step 1 says a rung may run it and the closing records the result.

##### Why: a rung may run it

Some checks run only mid-ladder, as in **fix: a missing fixture fails instead of passing**.

#### Dead-end cycles defined

- A cycle abandoned after its opening pushed still closes and lands. Its closing, titled with the
  cycle title plus " dead-end closing", keeps what is worth keeping, reverts the rest, and records
  what was tried, why it stopped, and what replaces it, then lands as a trapezoid like any closing.
- The title cap does not bind the suffix (wink, 2026-10-20).
- In `AGENTS.md` Close-out, `jj.md` Close-out shapes, and `prose.md`'s bookend titles.
- Open: whether a dead end's Land releases its bare version or reverts to the last release.
- First run: **test: the tests build the dr-1 fixture**, closed 2026-10-20.

##### Why: dead ends land

The cycle's agent-repo commits are on `main` and their `ochid:` trailers name its work-repo rungs,
so dropping the bookmark would leave them naming nothing, and landing keeps every rung reachable.

#### Warn rather than refuse

- Open, asked and unanswered (2026-10-24): wink's principle "warn rather than refuse", for a check
  whose failure may be a legitimate shape rather than a mistake, possibly a rule in
  `agent-data/code.md` beside the unwrap alert.
- Its uses so far, in `commit`: a title ending " closing" without `--closing` is warned about, a
  draft below `@-` and a closing with no bookmark are kept local with a line saying why, and a
  closing is never refused for an empty `@`.

##### Why: warn rather than refuse

We think a refusal of a legitimate shape sends the user to raw `jj`, which the tool exists to
retire, where a warning names what was done and leaves it reviewable before the push.

#### Continuation notes go in the closing

- Close-out step 7's notes are written before the closing commit, which carries them, so the
  work-repo is clean from the Land on and At rest's "both `@` empty" holds at the restart. A fact
  known only after the Land is not written: the note names what the next session checks, `main`
  at the closing, the bookmarks gone, the installed version's commit, and machine-local evidence,
  a `cmp` or the Land's output, lives in the agent-repo, published by the user's `squash-push -s
  a` after `/exit`. Provisional, on trial from **feat: vc-x1 land**.

##### Why: notes in the closing

Notes written after the Land have no clean home: a commit after it puts a non-cycle commit on the
trunk after the hard stop, and a squash into the closing rewrites the landmark just landed and
verified. The cost, notes written before the Land they describe, suits a close-out.

#### The exit-status rule is one form, and hooks guard it

- Working practices' Exit status becomes one form, the command under test bare and last, `set -o
  pipefail` first when piped, and the Rules index lists it and One command per invocation.
- The set carries its Claude Code hooks, `agent-data/bash-guard.sh`, `bash-allow.sh`, and
  `inhibit-sleep.sh`, with `agent-data/hooks.sh check|install|test`. Acquaint gains a step 2,
  Hooks, the check, the install the user's.
- `bash-allow.sh` names this family's commands and `inhibit-sleep.sh` needs systemd, so an adopter
  may carry other hooks, and `hooks.sh`'s lists are its own. From **feat: a hook enforces the
  shell rules**.

##### Why: hooks guard the rule

The rule was broken through a whole session with nothing failing, and a deny at the moment of the
slip is the one fix that does not rely on remembering it.

#### Not in it

Each run on its own:

- The record's home, `zDOING.md` in place of `TODO.md > ## In Progress`: **The cycle-record moves
  out of TODO.md into zDOING.md**.
- A rung inserted before pushed rungs: a `jj.md` recipe, once **lookup is tested on a reordered
  ladder** has its results.

### squash and commit take --exclude

vc-x1 0.85.16+fbe48200b7c8

Land a cycle whose last commit is already made: --onto fast-forwarded
to --source and pushed, and the cycle's bookmark deleted locally and
on `origin`, every check made before anything moves. `commit
--closing ... --land` lands the same way, the closing made first.

--source is a bookmark, the cycle's, or a revision, whose current
bookmark, else its nearest parent's above --onto, is the cycle's,
several refused with the list. Left out, it is the one local
bookmark besides --onto. --onto is a local bookmark at its
`origin` position that --source descends from, so a bushy tree lands
anywhere, and Land only fast-forwards: a merge is `commit
--closing`'s. --skip keeps a side of the cycle's bookmark, `local`,
`remote`, or `both`, and --delete-intermediate-bookmarks deletes the
bookmarks strictly between --onto and --source too. --dry-run makes
every check and says each step.

-s is required: `b` a dual workspace, the agent `main` published
with the trunk, and `p` a plain repo. `w` alone could publish
trailers naming agent commits not yet published, and `a` alone has
no cycle to land, so both are refused. The install stays `vc-x1
install`, after.

Usage: vc-x1 land [OPTIONS] --onto <BOOKMARK> --scope <SCOPE>

Options:
      --source <BM|REV>
          The cycle's last commit: a bookmark, the cycle's, or a revision, whose
          current bookmark, else its nearest parent's above `--onto`, is the
          cycle's [default: the one local bookmark besides `--onto`]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --onto <BOOKMARK>
          The bookmark landed on, fast-forwarded to `--source`: a local bookmark
          at its `origin` position that `--source` descends from

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --skip <SIDE>
          Which side of the cycle's bookmark is kept: `local`, `remote`, or
          `both`, none deleted

      --delete-intermediate-bookmarks
          Also delete the bookmarks on the commits strictly between `--onto` and
          `--source`, locally and on origin, as `--skip` allows: a stack of
          cycles landing together [default: named as merged and kept]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b`, or the repo itself for `-s
          p` [default: the current directory]

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required: `b|both` a dual workspace, or `p|por` a plain
          repo. `w` alone is refused, since it could publish trailers naming
          agent commits not yet published, and `a` alone, which has no cycle to
          land
          
          [possible values: both, por]

      --dry-run
          Dry run: show what would be done without executing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

348	(wink + agent, 2026-10-18, restructured 2026-10-20) Small rule fixes learned by running v0.3.0,

351	the rules below name. Each change is a `####` heading holding what is done, and its `#####` holds
352	why.

357	  `versioning.md` Dev artifact name is rewritten around the `[install]` table and the dev root.
358	- Land step 4 becomes `vc-x1 build`, a `vc-x1 run -- -V` smoke check, and `vc-x1 install`.
359	- Fast and full then differ only by `-- --include-ignored`, the fourteen `dr1_*` tests, and are
360	  identical once **dr-1 is built in Rust** drops their `#[ignore]`. What fast becomes is decided
361	  then.
362	
363	##### Why: never rename
364	
365	The rename's restore at Land changes the closing after its review, by a squash into a pushed
366	commit, and Land step 4 names no command.
367	
368	#### A local commit pair before every push
369	
370	- Per-rung flow steps 8 and 9 merge, since `commit` pushes what it commits: on the description
371	  review's go, `vc-x1 commit -s b --title --body` makes the pair and publishes it. With `--no-push`,
372	  or `[commit] push = false`, it keeps the pair local for a look at the commit itself, description
373	  and diff together, by `vc-x1 show -s both @-` or gitk, and `vc-x1 push -s b` publishes it after.
374	  A fix is edited and folded by `vc-x1 squash -s b`, a description fix by `squash -s b --title
375	  --body`.
376	- A commit made by hand, a draft below `@` with no description, is described in place by `vc-x1
377	  commit -s b -r REV --title --body`, its trailer stamped and its partner made, never by `jj
378	  describe`, and `--bookmark` moves the cycle's bookmark onto it past any nearer one.
379	- Step 6's work review stays ahead of it.
380	- Committing vs pushing is rewritten, `vc-x1 commit` committing both repos, `squash` continuing
381	  a rung, and `vc-x1 push` publishing, and `jj.md`'s vc-x1 push section follows.
382	- Re-describing: the rule becomes never by hand and never on a published commit, since the pair
383	  carries trailers from the start and `squash --title --body` is the sanctioned re-describe.
384	
385	##### Why: a local commit pair
386	
387	The last closing's review came after its push, so a change meant a remote rewrite and a
388	squash-push in both repos. Made as a pair, both trailers are known at commit and push carries no
389	description, so the reviewed commit is the published one. The work review stays first so a
390	description is not rewritten while the work still moves.
391	
392	#### The scope flags in the rules
393	
394	- Every `vc-x1` invocation in the agent-files carries its scope: `sync -s b` at the sync points,
395	  `commit -s b`, `squash -s b`, `push -s b` in the per-rung flow, and `squash-push -s a` for the
396	  user's squash-push, replacing `--scope=both` and `-R <agent-dir>`.
397	- Every argument is a flag, no positional: `commit -r REV`, `push -r REV --bookmark NAME`, and
398	  `squash-push --bookmark NAME`. Step 9's `vc-x1 commit -s b --title --body`, At rest's `squash-push
399	  -s a`, and `jj.md`'s vc-x1 push section's opening were brought current in this copy by **feat:
400	  push, commit, and squash-push take flags only**, the invocations alone, the Committing vs pushing
401	  rewrite still this proposal's.
402	- The rest of the commands too, by **feat: the other commands take flags only**: `versioning.md`'s
403	  adoption names `agent-files copy --from` and `diff --from`, and `hooks.sh`'s guard test names
404	  `install --dev`, `build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` being `build`, `install`, and `run`
405	  with `--dev` now. A rule that says `install-dev` says `install --dev`.
406	- And then by profile, by **feat: build, install, and run take --profile**: `--dev` retired to
407	  `--profile dev`, so `hooks.sh`'s guard test names `install --profile dev`, and a rule that says
408	  `install-dev` or `install --dev` says `install --profile dev`. The `[build]` and `[install]` keys a
409	  rule might name are `commands`, `dir`, and the `[profile.<name>]` tables.
410	
411	##### Why: the scope flags
412	
413	`-s` is required on the write commands and `sync` once **feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and run-dev**
414	lands, so the rules' invocations must carry it or fail.
415	
416	#### The closing is a trapezoid or linear, and converts
417	
418	- A multi-step cycle closes as a trapezoid by default or as linear on request, the closing commit
419	  carrying the shape, so nothing is reshaped at Land.
420	  - `vc-x1 commit --closing <BM|REV>`, naming the cycle's tip, onto the trunk, `--land`'s bookmark
421	    or `[cycle] trunk`, `main` when absent, makes the closing in the shape `--shape
422	    <trapezoid|linear>` names, else the `.vc-config.md` key `[cycle] closing-shape`, else
423	    trapezoid, and prints which decided.
424	  - Trapezoid is the merge of the trunk and the ladder's tip. Linear is a plain commit on the
425	    ladder, so the trunk carries one commit per rung, the shape the rules called keep separate,
426	    renamed.
427	  - The key is the project's preference, so each adopter sets its own, and one that sets nothing
428	    keeps the trapezoid.
429	  - Either converts to the other while the closing is a draft, before Land, by re-parenting the
430	    same closing: its change id, trailer, and, with the trunk unmoved, its tree are kept.
431	- Land is sync, then `commit --closing <BM|REV> --land [TRUNK]`, the fast-forward and the push,
432	  then `vc-x1 install`. To test the closing before it is published, it is made without `--land`,
433	  its release build, the candidate, installed off the PATH by `vc-x1 install --dir <DIR>` and
434	  tested by its path, and the candidate lands it, `<DIR>/vc-x1 land -s b --onto <TRUNK>`, and
435	  installs itself, `<DIR>/vc-x1 install`. The fast-forward lands the tree tested, so `cmp
436	  <DIR>/vc-x1` with the installed binary finds no difference, and the plain `vc-x1` is replaced
437	  only by what is on the trunk. The bookmark deleted is the one `--closing` names, or for a revision its
438	  current or nearest parent bookmark above the trunk, several refused with the list, and the
439	  branch's other bookmarks are left and named as merged. The trapezoid recipe goes,
440	  Close-out step 5 keeps the user's choice, the key its default, and carries it out by the flag,
441	  and `jj.md` Close-out shapes names the two shapes and why squash is not a shape.
442	
443	- The shape's name: with one rung the figure is a triangle, wink's observation (2026-10-20), so
444	  "trapezoid" names one case. The tool calls the operation `merge` and the result the merge
445	  close-out, and the rules' text could follow. `commit --closing` merges into the trunk as it is
446	  now, a bookmark read where it points, so a `main` that moved during the cycle no longer stops Land
447	  for a rebase. A linear closing cannot join a moved trunk without rewriting the reviewed ladder, so
448	  its Land refuses one.
449	
450	##### Why: a trapezoid by default, linear on request
451	
452	The trapezoid keeps every rung reachable while `git log --first-parent` reads one commit per cycle,
453	and it joins a moved trunk. Some prefer a straight history, which linear gives, and the choice is
454	made at the closing, so the shape is in the commit that was reviewed rather than a reshape at Land
455	made after it. Converting is cheap while the closing is a draft, so the choice is never final
456	before Land.
457	
458	#### A cycle's shape is its branch's commit count
459	
460	- [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)'s "A ladder that shrinks to one rung still closes as a
461	  ladder" goes: a branch with one commit above the trunk, the opening alone, is a single-step cycle,
462	  and `commit --closing <BM|REV>` finalizes that commit in place, the bare cycle title replacing the
463	  opening's, while more commits get the closing commit. Every closing names its tip, by the cycle's
464	  bookmark or a revision, `@-` the common one, and the count reads the branch, so there is no bare
465	  form, and `--dead-end` always makes the closing commit.
466	- Any commit on any line closes: a tip that is not `@-` is closed by a detour, `@` moving onto it
467	  and returning after, and the commits above it stay as they are.
468	- A parent wrong after the fact is fixed with `vc-x1 reparent`, never by closing again.
469	- Every cycle starts with `commit --opening`, a single-step cycle included: its bookmark is created
470	  and pushed at the trunk, and its one commit begins as the opening, the work squashed into it. So
471	  Opening step 2, the bookmark's creation and publication by `jj git push`, is `commit --opening`'s,
472	  and the step names it.
473	- The closing's title and body may be left out: the cycle title is read from the opening, and the
474	  body comes from `.vc-config.md`'s `[closing] body`.
475	
476	##### Why: the commit count
477	
478	The tool tells the shapes apart by counting, with no title to read, and a cycle need not decide its
479	shape before its first commit: it is single-step until a second commit makes it a ladder.
480	
481	#### A commit body is two plain paragraphs
482	
483	- The problem, then the solution opening "Solution:", ending with the pointer to the record where
484	  it is at that commit, "See details in zDOING.md." on a rung and "See details in zCLOSED.md." on
485	  the closing, which moves it, no bullets, and the rung subsection the full account: the entry **A
486	  commit body is an intro and a pointer to the record** in `## Todo`, its rule, specimens, and
487	  subsection change. The bookends stay pointers, "Opens the cycle ..." and "Closes the cycle ...",
488	  with the same pointer after them.
489	
490	##### Why: two paragraphs
491	
492	A `git log` reader gets what was wrong and what was done in two sentences, and the breakdown is
493	written once, in the record, rather than twice.
494	
495	#### Ladder labels from `[0]`
496	
497	- `notes.md` and the `cycle-model.md` specimen number the ladder's reference labels from `[0]`.
498	
499	##### Why: labels from zero
500	
501	Each label then equals its rung's version suffix.
502	
503	#### A rung may run the acceptance check
504	
505	- Close-out step 1 says a rung may run it and the closing records the result.
506	
507	##### Why: a rung may run it
508	
509	Some checks run only mid-ladder, as in **fix: a missing fixture fails instead of passing**.
510	
511	#### Dead-end cycles defined
512	
513	- A cycle abandoned after its opening pushed still closes and lands. Its closing, titled with the
514	  cycle title plus " dead-end closing", keeps what is worth keeping, reverts the rest, and records
515	  what was tried, why it stopped, and what replaces it, then lands as a trapezoid like any closing.
516	- The title cap does not bind the suffix (wink, 2026-10-20).
517	- In `AGENTS.md` Close-out, `jj.md` Close-out shapes, and `prose.md`'s bookend titles.
518	- Open: whether a dead end's Land releases its bare version or reverts to the last release.
519	- First run: **test: the tests build the dr-1 fixture**, closed 2026-10-20.
520	
521	##### Why: dead ends land
522	
523	The cycle's agent-repo commits are on `main` and their `ochid:` trailers name its work-repo rungs,
524	so dropping the bookmark would leave them naming nothing, and landing keeps every rung reachable.
525	
526	#### Warn rather than refuse
527	
528	- Open, asked and unanswered (2026-10-24): wink's principle "warn rather than refuse", for a check
529	  whose failure may be a legitimate shape rather than a mistake, possibly a rule in
530	  `agent-data/code.md` beside the unwrap alert.
531	- Its uses so far, in `commit`: a title ending " closing" without `--closing` is warned about, a
532	  draft below `@-` and a closing with no bookmark are kept local with a line saying why, and a
533	  closing is never refused for an empty `@`.
534	
535	##### Why: warn rather than refuse
536	
537	We think a refusal of a legitimate shape sends the user to raw `jj`, which the tool exists to
538	retire, where a warning names what was done and leaves it reviewable before the push.
539	
540	#### Continuation notes go in the closing
541	
542	- Close-out step 7's notes are written before the closing commit, which carries them, so the
543	  work-repo is clean from the Land on and At rest's "both `@` empty" holds at the restart. A fact
544	  known only after the Land is not written: the note names what the next session checks, `main`
545	  at the closing, the bookmarks gone, the installed version's commit, and machine-local evidence,
546	  a `cmp` or the Land's output, lives in the agent-repo, published by the user's `squash-push -s
547	  a` after `/exit`. Provisional, on trial from **feat: vc-x1 land**.
548	
549	##### Why: notes in the closing
550	
551	Notes written after the Land have no clean home: a commit after it puts a non-cycle commit on the
552	trunk after the hard stop, and a squash into the closing rewrites the landmark just landed and
553	verified. The cost, notes written before the Land they describe, suits a close-out.
554	
555	#### The exit-status rule is one form, and hooks guard it
556	
557	- Working practices' Exit status becomes one form, the command under test bare and last, `set -o
558	  pipefail` first when piped, and the Rules index lists it and One command per invocation.
559	- The set carries its Claude Code hooks, `agent-data/bash-guard.sh`, `bash-allow.sh`, and
560	  `inhibit-sleep.sh`, with `agent-data/hooks.sh check|install|test`. Acquaint gains a step 2,
561	  Hooks, the check, the install the user's.
562	- `bash-allow.sh` names this family's commands and `inhibit-sleep.sh` needs systemd, so an adopter
563	  may carry other hooks, and `hooks.sh`'s lists are its own. From **feat: a hook enforces the
564	  shell rules**.
565	
566	##### Why: hooks guard the rule
567	
568	The rule was broken through a whole session with nothing failing, and a deny at the moment of the
569	slip is the one fix that does not rely on remembering it.
570	
571	#### Not in it
572	
573	Each run on its own:
574	
575	- The record's home, `zDOING.md` in place of `TODO.md > ## In Progress`: **The cycle-record moves
576	  out of TODO.md into zDOING.md**.
577	- A rung inserted before pushed rungs: a `jj.md` recipe, once **lookup is tested on a reordered
578	  ladder** has its results.
579	
580	### squash and commit take --exclude

vc-x1 0.85.16+fbe48200b7c8

Land a cycle whose last commit is already made: --onto fast-forwarded
to --source and pushed, and the cycle's bookmark deleted locally and
on `origin`, every check made before anything moves. `commit
--closing ... --land` lands the same way, the closing made first.

--source is a bookmark, the cycle's, or a revision, whose current
bookmark, else its nearest parent's above --onto, is the cycle's,
several refused with the list. Left out, it is the one local
bookmark besides --onto. --onto is a local bookmark at its
`origin` position that --source descends from, so a bushy tree lands
anywhere, and Land only fast-forwards: a merge is `commit
--closing`'s. --skip keeps a side of the cycle's bookmark, `local`,
`remote`, or `both`, and --delete-intermediate-bookmarks deletes the
bookmarks strictly between --onto and --source too. --dry-run makes
every check and says each step.

-s is required: `b` a dual workspace, the agent `main` published
with the trunk, and `p` a plain repo. `w` alone could publish
trailers naming agent commits not yet published, and `a` alone has
no cycle to land, so both are refused. The install stays `vc-x1
install`, after.

Usage: vc-x1 land [OPTIONS] --onto <BOOKMARK> --scope <SCOPE>

Options:
      --source <BM|REV>
          The cycle's last commit: a bookmark, the cycle's, or a revision, whose
          current bookmark, else its nearest parent's above `--onto`, is the
          cycle's [default: the one local bookmark besides `--onto`]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --onto <BOOKMARK>
          The bookmark landed on, fast-forwarded to `--source`: a local bookmark
          at its `origin` position that `--source` descends from

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --skip <SIDE>
          Which side of the cycle's bookmark is kept: `local`, `remote`, or
          `both`, none deleted

      --delete-intermediate-bookmarks
          Also delete the bookmarks on the commits strictly between `--onto` and
          `--source`, locally and on origin, as `--skip` allows: a stack of
          cycles landing together [default: named as merged and kept]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b`, or the repo itself for `-s
          p` [default: the current directory]

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required: `b|both` a dual workspace, or `p|por` a plain
          repo. `w` alone is refused, since it could publish trailers naming
          agent commits not yet published, and `a` alone, which has no cycle to
          land
          
          [possible values: both, por]

      --dry-run
          Dry run: show what would be done without executing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

vc-x1 0.85.16+fbe48200b7c8

Commit the working copies as a rung's pair, one commit per repo of a
dual workspace, each stamped with the other's change id, and push it
in the same invocation, as `vc-x1 push` would.

The diff and the description are reviewed before the commit, so the
push publishes what was reviewed. --no-push keeps the commit local,
for a look at it by `vc-x1 show -s both @-` before `vc-x1 push`, and
`[commit] push = false` makes that the default, --push overriding it.

-r REV is the commit the description is for: `@` by default,
committed as the working copy, else `@-` or any draft below it,
described in place with no new commit and its trailer stamped, so a
commit made by hand becomes a rung's. A draft below `@-` is kept
local, since push publishes `@-`. Every argument is a flag: the old
positional is refused, naming -r.

--closing <BM|REV> closes the cycle whose tip it names, onto the trunk,
--land's or `[cycle] trunk`, `main` when absent: one commit above the
trunk is finalized in place, more get the closing commit, the merge of
the trunk and the tip. A tip that is not @- is closed by a detour, @
moving onto it and returning after. --land [TRUNK] lands it: the trunk
fast-forwarded and pushed and the closing's bookmark deleted, every
check first: the one named, or for a revision the current or nearest
parent bookmark above the trunk, several refused with the list.

-s is required: `b` makes both commits now, `w` the work half with
the agent half left to push, `a` the agent repo alone, unpaired, with
no trailer, and `p` a plain repo with no trailer. -R is optional and
says where. --body is the text, or @PATH to read it from a file.

Usage: vc-x1 commit [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE>

Options:
  -r, --revision <REV>
          The commit the description is for: `@` by default, committed as the
          working copy; `@-` or any draft below it is described in place with no
          new commit, its trailer stamped, so a commit made by hand becomes a
          rung's. Not with `--opening` or `--closing`

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b|w`, its root or either repo,
          or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the current directory]

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required: `w|work`, `a|agent`, `b|both`, or `p|por`
          
          [possible values: work, agent, both, por]

      --title <STR>
          Commit title, the Conventional Commit line; with `--opening` or
          `--closing` the bare cycle title [default with `--closing`: read from
          the opening]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --body <STR|@PATH>
          Commit body, the problem and its solutions, or @PATH to read it from a
          file [default with `--closing`: `[closing] body`, or the opening's for
          a single-step cycle]

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --closing <BM|REV>
          Close the cycle whose tip this names, a bookmark or a revision, onto
          the trunk, `--land`'s or `[cycle] trunk`: one commit above it is
          finalized in place, more get the closing commit, the merge of the
          trunk and the tip

      --dead-end
          With `--closing`, close the cycle as a dead end: the title ends "
          dead-end closing", always on a closing commit

      --opening [<BOOKMARK>]
          Make the work commit the cycle's opening: " opening" is appended to
          the bare cycle title, and BOOKMARK is created at the work `@-` and
          pushed to `origin` [default: the bare title's slug]

      --skip <SIDE>
          With `--opening`, what it leaves out: `local`, the bookmark is already
          at the work `@-` and is pushed; `remote`, it is created and not
          pushed; `both`, it is only checked. With `--land`, which side of the
          cycle's bookmark is kept: `local`, `remote`, or `both`, none deleted

          Possible values:
          - local:  The bookmark exists at the work `@-` already, so it is not
            created, only pushed
          - remote: The bookmark is created and not pushed
          - both:   The bookmark exists and is neither created nor pushed

      --land [<TRUNK>]
          With `--closing`, land the cycle on TRUNK, the closing's first parent:
          fast-forward it to the closing, push it, and delete the cycle's
          bookmark [default: `[cycle] trunk`, else `main`]

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run

Picked from `## Todo` as **undo takes back the last operation** (wink + agent, 2026-10-28), at the
opening of **push refuses rewriting the work trunk**, which this opening first carried and gave up
for this, wink's call (2026-10-28): undo is the safety net the push and squash rules lean on, so it
comes first. Run in the v0.3.1 form, wink's call (2026-10-28): every cycle from now on.

#### Problem

A vc-x1 write is local and so can be taken back, but only by raw jj, `jj op restore` in each repo,
two op logs for `-s b`, the agent-repo's moving with every session write. A `squash-push -s b` that
folds hours of uncommitted work into `@-` by mistake and pushes it leaves the work recoverable from
the op log and the remote rewritten, and getting both back means finding the right operation in each
repo by hand, restoring without clobbering the files on disk, and pushing the bookmark back past a
lease that the restore has made stale.

#### Solution

- Each vc-x1 run records itself in the op log jj already keeps, with no state file to disagree
  with it:
  - a run is one vc-x1 invocation, and it commits several operations, possibly in both repos
  - every operation a run commits carries one attribute, `args`, the key jj-cli keeps its own
    command line in, set by jj-lib's `Transaction::set_attribute`, so `jj op log` shows `args:
    vc-x1-dev 0.85.16-2+c594f1c06ba1 validate --fast` beside `args: jj diff --stat`
  - its value is the banner's program and build, then the arguments, the body left out and the
    title kept
  - it is set where each transaction starts: `Session::start_tx` and the three that start their
    own, the working-copy snapshot and the git HEAD and git refs imports.
- `jj op log` is the view of it: vc-x1 adds no reader of its own.
- No undo: the cycle stops after the record, a dead end, wink's (2026-10-29), the reasons in the
  Deliberation. A mistake is set aside going forward instead, a line's tail abandoned under a
  `dead-end-<id>` bookmark and a change reverted by a new commit, **abandon and revert set a mistake
  aside** in `TODO.md`.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with tests that:

- every write command's operations carry the run's one `args` line, in each repo it touches, the
  program and its build first, the title kept and the body left out.

#### Deliberation

- Undo first, wink's call (2026-10-28): the rules that stop refusing rewrites rest on everything
  local being undoable, so the net is built before the rules change. The push material went back
  to `## Todo` as **squash-push shows what it takes, and push follows jj**.
- The scenario that decided it, wink's (2026-10-28): a `squash-push -s b` folding hours of work by
  mistake and pushing it. jj keeps every earlier state, so nothing is lost locally, and the push is
  the part with no one-command way back.
- The op log is the record, not a file: the attributes travel with the operations, so the last run
  is found by reading the log, and what it pushed by comparing the remote-tracking bookmarks before
  and after it.
- The run record typed, wink's (2026-10-28): the attribute keys an enum and the id an integer, the
  strings jj stores made and read in one place, and a value that does not parse is no run of ours.
  The id is 128 bits, not 64: a u64 is ample while ids stay in one repo's local op log, but they
  will likely leave it, in a trailer, a message, or another engine, and the UUID v7 layout sorts
  by time at no visible cost, since people type a prefix. A random id needs no counter to
  coordinate, which a sequence would. The command is its own attribute, so undo can reason by
  command without parsing the command line, and the format version lets a later vc-x1 read an
  older record. Replaced by one `args` line on 2026-10-29, below.
- The record is one `args` line, wink's (2026-10-29), after reading `jj op log` beside `op --list`:

140-
141-The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
142-encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
143-Preparation**.
144-
145-This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
146-a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
147-number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
148-The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.
149-
150-- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
151-- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
152-- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)
153-
154-**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
155-starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
156-bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
157-needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
158-step without renumbering siblings.
159-
160-Disambiguation:
161-
162-- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
163-- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).
164-
165-**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:
166-
167-- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle

          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --body <STR|@PATH>
          Commit body, the problem and its solutions, or @PATH to read it from a
          file [default with `--closing`: `[closing] body`, or the opening's for
          a single-step cycle]

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --closing <BM|REV>
          Close the cycle whose tip this names, a bookmark or a revision, onto
          the trunk, `--land`'s or `[cycle] trunk`: one commit above it is
          finalized in place, more get the closing commit, the merge of the
          trunk and the tip

      --dead-end
          With `--closing`, close the cycle as a dead end: the title ends "
          dead-end closing", always on a closing commit

      --opening [<BOOKMARK>]
          Make the work commit the cycle's opening: " opening" is appended to
          the bare cycle title, and BOOKMARK is created at the work `@-` and
          pushed to `origin` [default: the bare title's slug]

      --skip <SIDE>
          With `--opening`, what it leaves out: `local`, the bookmark is already
          at the work `@-` and is pushed; `remote`, it is created and not
          pushed; `both`, it is only checked. With `--land`, which side of the
          cycle's bookmark is kept: `local`, `remote`, or `both`, none deleted

          Possible values:
          - local:  The bookmark exists at the work `@-` already, so it is not
            created, only pushed
          - remote: The bookmark is created and not pushed
          - both:   The bookmark exists and is neither created nor pushed

      --land [<TRUNK>]
          With `--closing`, land the cycle on TRUNK, the closing's first parent:
          fast-forward it to the closing, push it, and delete the cycle's
          bookmark [default: `[cycle] trunk`, else `main`]

      --bookmark <NAME>
          The bookmark to advance to the work commit, locally, any on the work
          commit's line, at or below it [default: the line's nearest, or
          `--opening`'s]

      --no-advance
          Leave the line's bookmark where it is, rather than advancing it to the
          work commit

      --no-push

2	
3	The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
4	its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
5	last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
6	commit's copy of the record.
7	
8	## Closed
9	
10	### feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run
11	
12	Picked from `## Todo` as **undo takes back the last operation** (wink + agent, 2026-10-28), at the
13	opening of **push refuses rewriting the work trunk**, which this opening first carried and gave up
14	for this, wink's call (2026-10-28): undo is the safety net the push and squash rules lean on, so it
15	comes first. Run in the v0.3.1 form, wink's call (2026-10-28): every cycle from now on.
16	
17	#### Problem
18	
19	A vc-x1 write is local and so can be taken back, but only by raw jj, `jj op restore` in each repo,
20	two op logs for `-s b`, the agent-repo's moving with every session write. A `squash-push -s b` that
21	folds hours of uncommitted work into `@-` by mistake and pushes it leaves the work recoverable from
22	the op log and the remote rewritten, and getting both back means finding the right operation in each
23	repo by hand, restoring without clobbering the files on disk, and pushing the bookmark back past a
24	lease that the restore has made stale.
25	
26	#### Solution
27	
28	- Each vc-x1 run records itself in the op log jj already keeps, with no state file to disagree
29	  with it:
30	  - a run is one vc-x1 invocation, and it commits several operations, possibly in both repos
31	  - every operation a run commits carries one attribute, `args`, the key jj-cli keeps its own
32	    command line in, set by jj-lib's `Transaction::set_attribute`, so `jj op log` shows `args:
33	    vc-x1-dev 0.85.16-2+c594f1c06ba1 validate --fast` beside `args: jj diff --stat`
34	  - its value is the banner's program and build, then the arguments, the body left out and the
35	    title kept
36	  - it is set where each transaction starts: `Session::start_tx` and the three that start their
37	    own, the working-copy snapshot and the git HEAD and git refs imports.
38	- `jj op log` is the view of it: vc-x1 adds no reader of its own.
39	- No undo: the cycle stops after the record, a dead end, wink's (2026-10-29), the reasons in the
40	  Deliberation. A mistake is set aside going forward instead, a line's tail abandoned under a
41	  `dead-end-<id>` bookmark and a change reverted by a new commit, **abandon and revert set a mistake
42	  aside** in `TODO.md`.
43	
44	#### Acceptance check
45	
46	`cargo test` passes with tests that:
47	
48	- every write command's operations carry the run's one `args` line, in each repo it touches, the
49	  program and its build first, the title kept and the body left out.
50	
51	#### Deliberation
52	
53	- Undo first, wink's call (2026-10-28): the rules that stop refusing rewrites rest on everything
54	  local being undoable, so the net is built before the rules change. The push material went back
55	  to `## Todo` as **squash-push shows what it takes, and push follows jj**.
56	- The scenario that decided it, wink's (2026-10-28): a `squash-push -s b` folding hours of work by
57	  mistake and pushing it. jj keeps every earlier state, so nothing is lost locally, and the push is
58	  the part with no one-command way back.
59	- The op log is the record, not a file: the attributes travel with the operations, so the last run
60	  is found by reading the log, and what it pushed by comparing the remote-tracking bookmarks before
61	  and after it.
62	- The run record typed, wink's (2026-10-28): the attribute keys an enum and the id an integer, the
63	  strings jj stores made and read in one place, and a value that does not parse is no run of ours.
64	  The id is 128 bits, not 64: a u64 is ample while ids stay in one repo's local op log, but they

139:## Suffix scheme
140-
141-The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
142-encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
143-Preparation**.
144-
145-This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
146-a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
147-number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
148-The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.
149-
150-- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
151-- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
152-- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)
153-
154-**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
155-starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
156-bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
157-needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
158-step without renumbering siblings.
159-
160-Disambiguation:
161-
162-- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
163-- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).
164-
165-**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:
166-
167-- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle

e3750ee feat: a hook enforces the shell rules

Working practices forbids masking a command's exit status, and the
agent broke the rule through a whole session with a trailing
`; echo rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, since nothing fails when it slips and the
rule is not in the Rules index.

Solution: a PreToolUse hook, `bash-guard.sh`, denies an echo of the
status and a cargo or vc-x1 command piped into a filter without
pipefail. The set carries it with the user's two other hooks and
`hooks.sh` to check, install, and test them, acquaint runs the check,
and the rule becomes one form, the command bare and last, listed in
the index. See details in zCLOSED.md.

The dr-1 fixture builder drives `push --title --body` and a bare
`squash-push`, forms vc-x1 no longer takes, so the fixture cannot be
built, and nothing noticed, since the tests read a fixture already built
and never run the builder.

Solution: the builder commits with `commit -s b --bookmark` and
squash-pushes with `-s a --yes`, and a test runs it against the binary
the test build makes, so full validation fails the day a command it
drives changes. See details in zCLOSED.md.

## Closed

### fix: the fixture builder drives commit

Not a `## Todo` entry: found at the Land of **feat: vc-x1 commit takes a revision** (2026-10-26),
when full validation on fwlaptop failed for want of `.fixtures/dr-1`.

#### Problem

`support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py` drives `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title ... --body ...` and
`vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent>`, two forms that went on 2026-10-20 with **feat: vc-x1 commit,
install, and run-dev**, so the dr-1 fixture cannot be built. Nothing noticed, since the fourteen
`dr1_*` tests read a built fixture and never run the builder: 3900x still holds one built on
2026-10-18, and fwlaptop, whose clone has none, is where the build was first needed.

#### Solution

- The builder commits each rung with `vc-x1 commit -s b --bookmark <bookmark>`, and squash-pushes
  the agent repo with `-s a --yes`.
- A test runs the builder against the vc-x1 the test build makes, so a change to the commands it
  drives fails validation the day it is made.

#### Acceptance check

With `.fixtures/` removed, `python3 support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py .fixtures --local` builds the
fixture, and `vc-x1 validate` passes, the fourteen `dr1_*` tests and the new builder test with it.

Result (2026-10-26, fwlaptop): passed. The builder test also fails against the builder as it was,
on `push`'s retired `--title`.

#### Deliberation

- Opened on the unlanded closing: the bookmark is created at the closing of **feat: vc-x1 commit
  takes a revision** rather than at `main`, and Land takes both cycles, wink's call (2026-10-26).
  - The closing stays as pushed, so no published commit is rewritten.
  - Bends [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)'s bookmark-on-`main`, for this cycle's opening only.

#### Ladder

- [fix: the fixture builder drives commit][f0] (done)

##### fix: the fixture builder drives commit

The builder follows the commands it drives, and a test keeps it following them.

- **dr1_builder_runs_against_this_vc_x1**, in `tests/cli_fixture_builder.rs`, runs
  `build-dr-1.py --local` into its own tempdir with `VC_X1` set to the binary the test build makes,
  and checks that both repos are colocated. It is ignored like the `dr1_*` tests, so full runs it
  and fast does not, at about 3.5 s.
  - `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` point at the tempdir, by `tests/common`'s `isolate_config`, now
    public, so init's Claude Code symlink lands there and not under the user's home.
  - Spawning `python3` is entry 4 of the spawn register in `clippy.toml`, test fixture setup,
    widened to name it.

#### Land is the sequence, and `vc-x1 land` its integrate step

- Land stays the rules' word for the whole sequence that makes a cycle permanent: sync, integrate,
  install. `vc-x1 land` names the command alone, its integrate step: `--onto` fast-forwarded and
  pushed and the cycle's bookmark deleted, with no sync and no install. A rule writes "Land" for the
  sequence and `vc-x1 land` for the command, and never one for the other.

  Terminology, Sync's "Land syncs", Close-out step 6, and `jj.md`'s Land.

  command and not the sequence: nothing is installed, and the cycle is permanent only when it
  reaches the trunk.

Land also installs and assumes `main`, so a reader of either takes the word to mean what the other
does. Installing only from the trunk keeps the rule above, that the plain `vc-x1` is replaced only
by what is on the trunk.

#### Land is the sequence, and `vc-x1 land` its integrate step

- Land stays the rules' word for the whole sequence that makes a cycle permanent: sync, integrate,
  install. `vc-x1 land` names the command alone, its integrate step: `--onto` fast-forwarded and
  pushed and the cycle's bookmark deleted, with no sync and no install. A rule writes "Land" for the
  sequence and `vc-x1 land` for the command, and never one for the other.
- Land is onto the trunk, `[cycle] trunk`, `main` when absent, where the rules now assume `main`:
  Terminology, Sync's "Land syncs", Close-out step 6, and `jj.md`'s Land.
- `vc-x1 land --onto` a bookmark that is not the trunk, a stack of cycles landing together, is the
  command and not the sequence: nothing is installed, and the cycle is permanent only when it
  reaches the trunk.

##### Why: two names for two things

`vc-x1 land` integrates onto any `--onto` and leaves the install to `vc-x1 install`, while the rules'
Land also installs and assumes `main`, so a reader of either takes the word to mean what the other
does. Installing only from the trunk keeps the rule above, that the plain `vc-x1` is replaced only
by what is on the trunk.

content.text:
Two Todos are moot:

- **undo refuses clone and init runs** (`TODO.md:204`): this would make `undo` refuse to take back a `clone` or `init` run, and mark those runs in `undo --list`.
- **undo across clones** (`TODO.md:214`): this would let one clone find and undo a run made in another, using a `vc-x1-run: <id>` trailer on the run's commits.

Both exist only to refine a `vc-x1 undo` command, and that command was never built: **feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run** stopped as a dead end after adding the run record, and **abandon and revert set a mistake aside** replaced it.

One fact in **undo across clones** still holds without undo: the op log is local to `.jj`, so a clone starts with none of the original's operations, while change ids and `ochid:` trailers carry over. **vc-x1 stamps no user, host, or workspace on its operations** may be a better home for that, but I haven't read that entry yet. I'd delete both and move that fact there if it fits.

content.content:
180	### The run record misses workspace init
181	
182	(agent, 2026-10-29) A `clone` run's first operation in each repo, jj-lib's `add workspace
183	'default'`, carries no run record, since it is made before vc-x1 opens a transaction. The record is
184	set at four places, `Session::start_tx` and the snapshot and the two git imports, and workspace

### The run record misses workspace init

(agent, 2026-10-29) A `clone` run's first operation in each repo, jj-lib's `add workspace
'default'`, carries no run record, since it is made before vc-x1 opens a transaction. The record is
set at four places, `Session::start_tx` and the snapshot and the two git imports, and workspace
init is a fifth. Seen in a fresh `vc-x1-dev clone`, whose other three operations per repo carry
the run.

- Tag it, or treat the operation before a run's first as the run's base, which is what an undo
  restores to either way.
- `init` makes the same operation and is the other case to check.

### vc-x1 stamps no user, host, or workspace on its operations

(agent, 2026-10-29) In `jj op log` raw jj's operations read `wink@3900x default@` and vc-x1's read
`@`, with no user or host, and its snapshots carry no workspace either. In this work-repo 543
operations are raw jj's, 427 vc-x1's with a workspace, and 389 vc-x1's without.

- Set the user and host through jj-lib's settings, as jj-cli does, so vc-x1's operations read as
  jj's own, the run record saying which run made them.
- The snapshot path sets the workspace as the transactions do.
- A missing stamp tells vc-x1's operations from raw jj's today, and is how a stable vc-x1's
  untagged ones were recognized. The run record replaces that test.

### undo refuses clone and init runs

(wink + agent, 2026-10-29) In a fresh clone the one run `undo --list` offers is the clone, and
undoing it would restore each repo to its first operation, no remote and nothing fetched. There is
no state before a `clone` or an `init` worth returning to, and removing the directory is its undo.

- `undo` refuses a run whose command is `clone` or `init`, naming why, and `undo --list` marks it
  or leaves it out.
- For **feat: undo takes back the last vc-x1 run** or a cycle after it.

### undo across clones

(wink + agent, 2026-10-28, confirmed 2026-10-29) The op log is local to `.jj` and never pushed, so a
run made in one clone cannot be listed or undone from another. A fresh `vc-x1-dev clone` of this
pair begins both op logs at the clone, none of the original's operations carried. Commits carry
their change ids, `c594f1c0`, `c1e9e653`, and `de2e9af7` identical in both, so `ochid:` trailers
resolve in a clone.

- The idea: a `vc-x1-run: <id>` trailer on the commits a run makes, so a clone finds a run's
  commits by their trailer where it has no op log to read.
- What a clone could undo is open: the commits and pushes a trailer finds, not the local operations
  only the original saw.

# The package name is the installed binary's name and never
# changes: a cycle's validation installs under its own root,

# dev build (a suffixed version) never replaces the stable
# `vc-x1` on the PATH. The promotion is the plain `cargo install`

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`

# clippy.toml's register entry 6 closes (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
jj-lib = "0.46"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
# The rng jj-lib's `SecureConfig` takes to mint a repo's config id,
# at jj-lib 0.46's versions so the types are its own, seeded the way
# jj-cli seeds it (src/jj/session.rs `load_repo_config`).
rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

vc-x1 0.85.17+9109352e38fc

Publish a rung's pair: the work commit on its bookmark and the
agent commit on `main`. Push carries no description and writes
none, so what was reviewed is what goes out.

`commit` makes the pair, both commits now (-s b) or the work
half with its trailer naming the agent @ (-s w). Push publishes
the work @-, so new work in @ is left as it is, and it refuses
a work @- with no `ochid:` trailer, which is not a pair's commit.

The halves are independent, each trailer being fixed before
push runs, so -s b is -s a then -s w, the order the pair is
completed in:
  - agent  complete the partner by the state found: fold the
           journal into a committed one, or commit it as the
           partner when pending or the agent repo changed;
           then squash-push main
  - work   restamp the unpublished work commit if its trailer
           does not name the partner, then set and push
           <bookmark>

-s is required: `b` both halves, `a` the agent half, `w` the work
half, `p` a plain repo's @- on its bookmark. -R is optional and
says where. --bookmark is the line's unless named, as a check or
as a new name created at @- and pushed tracked.

-r names another commit, already made, and a name alone goes out
for it, no pair: the one bookmark at it, or --bookmark's, that
bookmark or a new one created there. The working copy and the
root are refused, and so is a REV of several commits.

Every argument is a flag: the old positional is refused, naming
--bookmark or -r, the one it was.

Rerunning is always safe: a half whose work is done finds nothing
to do. A half that fails before its own push restores the repo it
touched via `jj op restore`.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE>

Options:
  -r, --revision <REV>
          The commit to publish, one: `@-` publishes the pair, any other a name
          alone [default: `@-`]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --bookmark <NAME>
          The remote's name for it: a bookmark on the line, moved there, one
          already at REV, or a new name, created there [default: the line's
          bookmark, or the one at REV]

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b|w|a`, its root or either
          repo, or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the current directory]

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required: `w|work`, `a|agent`, `b|both`, or `p|por`
          
          [possible values: work, agent, both, por]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

  -y, --yes
          Pass the `--step` gates without asking

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

content.text:
The squash into 0.85.17 is ready locally, but it hasn't run because it rewrites `main` on `origin`, so I need your explicit go. Full validation passes on the prepared tree.

**What's prepared**
- The version is back to 0.85.17.
- `zDOING.md` reads `_None._` with no cycle in progress.
- The undo Todo work is folded into the 0.85.17 record in `zCLOSED.md`, including a note that this bends the rule against rewriting a published commit, for this commit alone.

**What the go runs**
1. `vc-x1 squash -s b --yes`, with the new description below.
2. `vc-x1 push -s b`, which force-moves `main` on `origin` in both repos.
3. `vc-x1 install`, because the installed binary still reports `9109352e`.

**The cost**
- Commit `9109352e` is replaced on `main`, though its change id and `ochid:` trailer stay the same.
- Any other clone that already fetched it, such as fwlaptop, has to sync past the rewrite.
- I recommend doing it anyway if no other clone has built on that commit, since it only landed minutes ago and nothing on `origin` sits on top of it.

**New description** (the title is unchanged)
```
chore: drop session.rs.orig and define Land in v0.3.1

src/jj/session.rs.orig is tracked and nothing reads it, the word Land
names both the rules' whole sequence and the vc-x1 land command, the
continuation notes hold finished items and a damaged leftover, and two
Todos refine an undo that was never built.

Solution: delete the file, carry the two meanings of Land apart in the
agent-files v0.3.1 proposal, delete the two Todos with their one lasting
fact moved, and reset the notes. See details in zCLOSED.md.
```

Do you want me to go ahead with the squash, the push and the install?
